changeSet.author: solarcalc
changeSet.comment: Drop rows carrying no price at all. The setup wizard used to post field names the API did not know, so every profile created through onboarding got one all-null snapshot.

delete.where: electricity_price IS NULL AND feed_in_tariff IS NULL AND petrol_price IS NULL AND oil_reference_cost IS NULL AND gas_reference_cost IS NULL

changeSet.comment: A null period meant "the profile default", i.e. in effect for all of history. The earliest possible start month preserves exactly that role.
changeSet.sql: UPDATE price_snapshot SET period = '1970-01' WHERE period IS NULL OR TRIM(period) = ''
changeSet.comment: The old index was not unique and nothing checked for duplicates, so a profile may already hold several rows for the same period — including several former null-period rows that just collapsed onto 1970-01. Keep the most recently created one; without this the unique constraint below would abort the whole migration and the app would not start.
changeSet.sql: DELETE FROM price_snapshot WHERE id NOT IN ( SELECT keep_id FROM ( SELECT MAX(id) AS keep_id FROM price_snapshot GROUP BY energy_profile_id, period ) AS keepers )

changeSet.author: solarcalc
changeSet.comment: Two snapshots for the same start month made the resolver's single-result lookup throw at read time. One start month, one entry.

changeSet.author: solarcalc
changeSet.comment: Redundant once the unique constraint above exists: both start with energy_profile_id, so the new one also carries the foreign key. It has to be dropped last for exactly that reason — MariaDB refuses while it is the only index backing the FK.
